brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases piece:0,0,0 / piece:1,0,0 / piece:0,1,0 plus a half base piece:0,-1,0 (half-w), with open faces capped (capOpenFaces) and joints bolted (lockJoints).

bin:0,0,0 (hex-bin-full-div3, 3 compartments) and bin:0,1,0 (hex-bin-full-div2, 2 compartments). Both are drop-in trays that hang on their rims. Props for screws/nuts were tried but hid under the rims, so they were removed; the bins are empty.
notch:0#-1,0#notch0 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) fills the empty position beside the bases at (-1,0). The drawer frame is placed; I did not separately verify the drawer's pull-out motion.
handle:1,0,0;top sits on cover:1,0,0 (full, top) with its inserts, on the east block.
The configurator checks fit and collisions only. The build is compact (about 4 cells, one handle), but weight, grip comfort and material durability are not verified.

finish.summary: Built a compact hex-base electronics organizer: a 4-block base (three full, one half) with two removable compartment bins (3-compartment and 2-compartment), a notch drawer frame on the west side, and a carry handle on a top cover of the east block. The check reads ok with meshClash clear and no issues. Props were removed because the small-part props sat hidden under the bin rims. Portability is only partly shown: the handle and compact size are there, but the configurator cannot judge weight or grip.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
